title: Moving Your Pieces
steps: Roll the dice by tapping the dice cup.
Tap a piece that can move — its legal destinations highlight in green.
Tap a highlighted square to move the piece there.
A waiting piece enters on the square the roll carries it to.
If no piece can use the roll, the turn passes automatically.
label: invented

title: Captures and Rosettes
steps: Landing on a shared square held by an opponent sends that piece home.
Landing on any rosette grants another roll.
The central rosette is safe: an opponent there cannot be captured, and your piece cannot be taken from it.
The odds panel shows your chance to capture on the next roll.
Doubling raises the stake; a doubled stake changes what the match is worth.
label: invented

title: Winning and the Circuit
steps: Bear off all seven pieces to win the match; the exact roll is needed for the last step.
If the loser has borne off nothing, some taverns double the loss (a gammon).
In the circuit you pay a buy-in at each tavern; matches pay the tavern's minimum stake.
When your purse cannot cover the next buy-in, the run ends.
Between matches, buy omens or pay to learn an opponent's tell.
label: invented
